batch_strategy: Select connected condition contrasts that distinguish endpoint-specific loading responses, unsupported strong-eluent bends, and scaffold-dependent weak-eluent curves. Use measured anchors to make new labels interpretable, avoid duplicate recorded tuples within the batch, and freeze all 32 point predictions before measurement. Prior acquisition errors motivate questions but are not treated as current residuals; quantile widths are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

hypotheses.content: Loading responses depend on both endpoint and mobile-phase composition. Several measured series shift onset substantially while completion changes little, but other scaffolds change completion or show different loading responses at different compositions. A single shared loading adjustment is insufficient.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts and missing midpoints can teach conditional endpoint responses across alcohols, amines, ketones, and ketoesters. Repeated-input variation limits causal interpretation and makes local anchoring important.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the predicted high-load onset upticks for m128, m200, and m135 survive measurement, and do m19, m25, and m203 develop their stronger loading responses only at weaker mobile phases?

hypotheses.content: m194 shows a large completion dependence on loading at both 1/1 and 2/1, with comparatively small onset changes. The loading at which the completion extension develops, and whether pure EA removes it at high loading, remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest low-load 1/1 completion was overpredicted by 19.44 mL at acquisition. A midpoint and a fixed-high-loading solvent extension distinguish smooth interpolation, a concentrated loading transition, and composition dependence without assigning an unsupported physical mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 1/1 and 100 uL, is completion closer to the short low-load interval or the extended high-load interval, and does high-load completion return to about 10 mL in pure EA?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent response bends must be evaluated by scaffold and endpoint. The previously predicted m129, m11, and m211 completion maxima were not supported, while m27 has a measured completion maximum near 2/1. Remaining maxima and minima cannot be classified from solvent-strength priors alone.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected solvent labels can repair unsupported interpolation while preserving real nonmonotonic behavior. The selected carbonyl, ester, and hydrocarbon examples test whether corrections transfer across chemical environments or require local conditioning.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which proposed strong-eluent maxima in m185, m34, m10, and m215 are measured, and do m73 and m197 retain their predicted intervening completion minima?

hypotheses.content: The previous point-prediction endpoint crossings in m156, m91, m17, and m18 were not reproduced as crossed measured endpoints. Their acquisition errors involved different endpoint directions, indicating local joint-response failures rather than one universal endpoint offset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Measurements of connected early-eluting conditions can constrain both endpoints and their interval without relying on clipping. The new m156 and m71 pairs test remaining abrupt strong-eluent changes even though their current point predictions are ordered.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m156's predicted pure-EA completion expansion real, and does m71 actually show the large predicted onset decrease between pure EA and 2/1 at fixed loading?

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent response shapes vary across aromatic carbonyl environments: some measured ketones retain an early or nearly stationary onset while completion increases, whereas others move both endpoints substantially. Functional-group counts and hydrophobicity alone do not establish the response shape.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m41 and m169 sequences test different proposed endpoint-response shapes in ordinary neutral chemistry, while acetophenone supplies a useful reference. This broadens learning beyond the recent donor and strong-eluent failure regions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m41 plateau from 20/1 to 50/1, does m169 show increasing completion at almost fixed onset through 10/1 and 20/1, and does acetophenone flatten at 50/1?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes supported endpoint-specific loading effects but reduced the value of repeatedly sampling already completed series. m209 at 20/1 now has V1 decreasing from 26.92 to 18.81 to 14.43 mL across loading, while V2 decreases only modestly from 53.89 to 51.67 to 50.83 mL. m45 already shows substantial onset separation at 10/1, so that effect does not arise only beyond 10/1. The predicted m114 high-load onset upticks were not measured; its completion predictions were very close. I therefore move those completed series out of this batch and test analogous unresolved bends in other scaffolds. m194 provided the clearest new completion-loading failure: at 1/1, low-load V2 was 10.34 mL versus 27.33 mL at high loading, motivating its missing midpoint and pure-EA extension. m92's new low-load labels strengthened composition dependence while its repeated-input variation still prevents a simple causal loading rule. The m129, m11, and m211 strong-eluent maxima disappeared on measurement, whereas m27's new 1/1 result places its observed completion maximum nearer 2/1. All selected endpoint crossings became ordered measured pairs, but the needed corrections differed by endpoint. These findings favor connected local measurements over blanket monotonicity or ordering-based acquisition. The quoted past errors are acquisition-time errors, not residuals of the current retrained model.
batch_rationale: The 32 choices are distinct supplied candidate IDs, have condition novelty 1, contain no duplicate recorded tuples within the batch, and duplicate no pending experiments. Every selected point prediction is frozen in its reason. The batch combines three useful forms of evidence. First, loading midpoints, loading extremes, and matched solvent extensions test when onset and completion respond differently, including m194's large newly observed completion contrast and m92's composition-dependent response. Second, strong-eluent sequences test unsupported maxima and minima across carbonyls, an ester, fluorinated benzene, and neutral aromatic systems; measured m27 and m4 behavior prevents assuming that every inversion is an artifact. Third, the m41 and m169 curves and acetophenone extension cover ordinary weak-eluent response regions where generalization requires distinguishing onset plateaus from simultaneous movement of both endpoints. Several selections may confirm an accurate prediction; their value is in discriminating response shapes and preventing inappropriate transfer of recent corrections. The indene midpoint explicitly addresses interpolation near conflicting repeated records without claiming that one new label can identify omitted variables or measurement noise. Sample loading is interpreted through the supplied density and volume conditions; loading_amount_mg remains their derived product. No absent concentration, flow, pH, or other column variables are assumed. Quantile widths did not determine the batch, and V2 minus V1 is treated as the elution interval. These labels are intended to improve retrained V1/V2 prediction across the Row-distribution, not to maximize retention or optimize the selected separations.
